<?php
fscanf(STDIN, "%d %d", $l, $r);

function reflect($n) {
    $s = strval($n);
    $len = strlen($s);
    $res = '';
    for ($i = 0; $i < $len; $i++) {
        $digit = intval($s[$i]);
        $res .= strval(9 - $digit);
    }
    // remove leading zeros
    $res = ltrim($res, '0');
    if ($res === '') return 0;
    return intval($res);
}

function weight($n) {
    $ref = reflect($n);
    return $n * $ref;
}

$best = 0;

// candidate 1: r
$best = max($best, weight($r));

// candidate 2: number with all 9s of same length as r, but not exceeding r
$len = strlen(strval($r));
$all9 = intval(str_repeat('9', $len));
if ($all9 >= $l && $all9 <= $r) {
    $best = max($best, weight($all9));
}

// candidate 3: smallest number with one more digit (10^(len-1))
$pow = 1;
for ($i = 1; $i < $len; $i++) $pow *= 10; // 10^(len-1)
if ($pow >= $l && $pow <= $r) {
    $best = max($best, weight($pow));
}

// candidate 4: l
$best = max($best, weight($l));

echo $best . PHP_EOL;
?>

<?php
// Read input
$line = trim(fgets(STDIN));
list($l, $r) = array_map('intval', explode(' ', $line));

function reflect_number($n) {
    $s = strval($n);
    $len = strlen($s);
    $res = '';
    for ($i = 0; $i < $len; $i++) {
        $digit = intval($s[$i]);
        $res .= strval(9 - $digit);
    }
    // Remove leading zeros
    $res = ltrim($res, '0');
    if ($res === '') $res = '0';
    return intval($res);
}

function weight($n) {
    $ref = reflect_number($n);
    return $n * $ref;
}

$maxWeight = 0;

// Helper to update maxWeight for a specific n if within range
function try_n($n, $l, $r, &$maxWeight) {
    if ($n < $l || $n > $r) return;
    $w = weight($n);
    if ($w > $maxWeight) $maxWeight = $w;
}

// Check boundaries
try_n($l, $l, $r, $maxWeight);
try_n($r, $l, $r, $maxWeight);

// Generate candidates of form 10^k and 10^k - 1 around the range
for ($k = 0; $k <= 10; $k++) {
    $pow10 = 1;
    for ($i = 0; $i < $k; $i++) $pow10 *= 10;

    // n = 10^k
    try_n($pow10, $l, $r, $maxWeight);

    // n = 10^k - 1
    if ($pow10 > 1) {
        try_n($pow10 - 1, $l, $r, $maxWeight);
    }
}

// Additionally, check numbers formed by leading '9's followed by zeros within the range
// e.g., 90, 900, 990, etc.
for ($k = 1; $k <= 10; $k++) {
    $pow10 = 1;
    for ($i = 0; $i < $k; $i++) $pow10 *= 10;

    // 9 * 10^(k-1)
    $candidate = 9 * ($pow10 / 10);
    if ($candidate >= 1) {
        try_n($candidate, $l, $r, $maxWeight);
        // candidate - 1
        try_n($candidate - 1, $l, $r, $maxWeight);
    }
}

echo $maxWeight . PHP_EOL;
?>

$maxWeight = 0;

$maxWeight = max($maxWeight, weight($r));

// candidate 3: number with all 9s of same length as r
$lenR = strlen(strval($r));
$all9 = intval(str_repeat('9', $lenR));
if ($all9 >= $l && $all9 <= $r) {
    $maxWeight = max($maxWeight, weight($all9));

// candidate 4: number with all 9s of length lenR-1 (if possible)
if ($lenR > 1) {
    $all9prev = intval(str_repeat('9', $lenR - 1));
    if ($all9prev >= $l && $all9prev <= $r) {
        $maxWeight = max($maxWeight, weight($all9prev));
    }
}

// candidate 5: adjust around all9 within range
if ($all9 > $r) {
    // try r with lower digits set to 9
    $s = strval($r);
    $len = strlen($s);
    for ($i = 0; $i < $len; $i++) {
        if ($s[$i] != '9') {
            $candidate = substr($s, 0, $i) . '9' . str_repeat('9', $len - $i - 1);
            $n = intval($candidate);
            if ($n >= $l && $n <= $r) {
                $maxWeight = max($maxWeight, weight($n));
            }
        }
    }
}

Write a program in PHP to solve this programming problem:
Description: For each positive integer n consider the integer ψ(n) which is obtained from n by replacing every digit a in the decimal notation of n with the digit (9  -  a). We say that ψ(n) is the reflection of n. For example, reflection of 192 equals 807. Note that leading zeros (if any) should be omitted. So reflection of 9 equals 0, reflection of 91 equals 8.Let us call the weight of the number the product of the number and its reflection. Thus, the weight of the number 10 is equal to 10·89 = 890.Your task is to find the maximum weight of the numbers in the given range [l, r] (boundaries are included).
Input Specification: Input contains two space-separated integers l and r (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ 109) — bounds of the range.
Output Specification: Output should contain single integer number: maximum value of the product n·ψ(n), where l ≤ n ≤ r. Please, do not use %lld specificator to read or write 64-bit integers in C++. It is preferred to use cout (also you may use %I64d).

Sample Input:
3 7
Sample Output:
20

Sample Input:
1 1
Sample Output:
8

Sample Input:
8 10
Sample Output:
890

Notes: NoteIn the third sample weight of 8 equals 8·1 = 8, weight of 9 equals 9·0 = 0, weight of 10 equals 890.Thus, maximum value of the product is equal to 890.
Take input from standard input and output to standard output
